ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against: French regulator watchlists (ACPR, TRACFIN), European Union consolidated financial sanctions list (FIU FICO), UN Security Council consolidated list, FATF black-list/grey-list jurisdictions, EU and national PEP databases (national elected officials, ministerial cabinet members, members of constitutional bodies, senior magistrates, and high-ranking military officers), and relevant OFAC SDN lists for cross-border USD clearing. Screening must occur at pre-engagement, pre-incorporation, at the signing of share subscription agreements, at director appointment, and on a rolling 90-day basis for the first year. All hits require senior management escalation, enhanced due diligence, and potential rejection without a satisfactory lawful commercial explanation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) and Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (RNCS) via Infogreffe
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French company names may be expressed in any language, but the statutory legal name of the SAS must be written in Latin characters for registration and publication. If a foreign-language name is used, a French transliteration or a French trade name may be required for mandatory public filings. All supporting documents must be in French or accompanied by a sworn French translation (traduction assermentée). The name must not contain terms contrary to French public policy, morality, or professional rules, and must not mislead as to the object of the company.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected by the Greffe du Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés, the applicant may file a preliminary administrative appeal (recours gracieux) with the Greffe within 30 days of the written refusal. If no favourable response is received, the applicant may file a formal judicial appeal (recours contentieux) before the Tribunal de Commerce within 30 days of the administrative decision or expiry of the administrative response deadline. If the Tribunal de Commerce dismisses the appeal, an appeal may be brought before the Cour d'appel, and ultimately before the Cour de Cassation on questions of law. The applicant must correct the name or alter the denommination and must allow for the reserved-name release period before resubmitting. A parallel trademark search must be conducted at INPI, and a French national trademark application may be filed to preserve availability; oppositions are handled under the Code de la propriété intellectuelle.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Registered as a completion-dealt activity, virtual office space is permissible only through a licensed domiciliary agent (société de domiciliation) holding a physical commercial address in France and entering into a written annual domiciliation contract. The virtual office may satisfy the registered office requirement for formation, but it is materially insufficient for the substance test under this high-voltage substation contracting scope. The company must maintain permanent operating premises in France (owned, leased, or under commercial service contract) with exclusive access, local personnel records, equipment storage, and documentation for permit inspections.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Elevated. Mandatory documented annual compliance inspections by the Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement, URSSAF, the labour inspectorate, and the local Préfecture, with a realistic risk of unannounced on-site inspections during active substation installation works. Statistical data from prior electrical-construction projects indicates an above-60% probability of at least one unannounced site visit within the first operational year when the enterprise holds an electrical contractor license and operates under individual site permits.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Title II, Chapter VII: Articles L.227-1 through L.227-24 (Société par Actions Simplifiée); general corporate provisions Articles L.210-1 through L.210-10; Civil Code Articles 1832-1844-17; implementing provisions in Décret n° 67-236 of 23 March 1967 (codified at R.227-1 et seq. and R.210-1 et seq. of the Code de commerce).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle) — Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises, which transmits the dossier to the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) and to the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) kept by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Dossier unique d'immatriculation consisting of the electronic formalité M0 (Cerfa n° 15679*) filed through the INPI Guichet Unique portal, leading to RNE registration and issuance of the K-bis extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for an SAS; the share capital is freely fixed in the articles but must be fully subscribed. Cash contributions must be released in accordance with the articles; funds paid before registration must be deposited in a blocked escrow account (compte bloqué) with a French credit institution, Caisse des Dépôts or notarial escrow, with release to the President only upon RCS registration. Contributions in kind require a statutory auditor's report (rapport du commissaire aux apports) unless waived under law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST ORGANIZING RESOLUTION OF THE SAS IN FORMATION, [Location], [Date]. The founding shareholders, acting as the initial corporate organ: 1. Subscription of shares. The statutory share capital, freely fixed at [amount], is declared fully subscribed and divided into [number] shares; in-kind contributions are definitively approved. 2. Registered office. The premises at [address] are adopted as the statutory registered office, and the representative is empowered to file domiciliation declarations. 3. Officers. [Name] is appointed President, and [Name], if any, is appointed Directeur Général, with statutory powers. 4. Mandate. The President is authorized to publish the incorporation notice, file the M0 registration with the INPI Guichet Unique, and open company bank accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the articles of association and deposit of share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders' legal counsel or French notary (optional); French credit institution or Caisse des Dépôts for the blocked escrow account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and sign the statuts, signed by all shareholders. Where in-kind contributions are made, appoint a commissaire aux apports to issue the valuation report. Open a temporary blocked account in the name of the company in formation, deposit the cash subscription funds, and obtain the attestation de dépôt des fonds de la société en formation.
required_dossiers: Statuts signed by all founding shareholders
Nomination deed of the President and, if any, the Directeur Général
Commissaire aux apports valuation report for in-kind contributions
Bank certificate of capital deposit (attestation de dépôt des fonds)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the blocked account, select another authorized credit institution or notarial escrow; any adjustment of the capital allocation requires a supplementary act signed by all shareholders amending the statuts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the incorporation notice in a legal advertisement gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Habilitated Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) in the department of the registered office, selected from the official list published by the prefecture.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transmit the draft avis de constitution containing the corporate name, legal form, share capital, registered office, corporate object, President, and anticipated RCS registration number. Pay the publication fee and obtain the attestation de parution evidencing the insertion.
required_dossiers: Draft legal notice of incorporation (avis de constitution)
Copy of the signed statuts
Identification details of the shareholders and the President
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL requires correction of the notice, submit an amended text for republication and obtain a new attestation de parution; the corrected notice must remain consistent with the final signed statuts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of the single filing dossier, beneficial owner declaration and registered office justification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company legal counsel; documents to be submitted electronically through the INPI Guichet Unique portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the electronic formalité M0, annex the signed statuts, attestation de parution, attestation de dépôt des fonds, justification of enjoyment of the registered office, declaration of beneficial owners (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs), identity documents of the legal representatives, and any power of attorney authorizing the filer.
required_dossiers: Dossier M0 electronic form (Cerfa n° 15679*)
Power of attorney where a representative files the application
Justification de jouissance du siège social (lease title or certificate of the legal representative)
Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs (DBE)
Identity documents and proof of residence of the President and legal representatives
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the portal flags an incompleteness, rectify the dossier online within the allotted rectification period without re-paying the droits de greffe where the initial filing was substantially complete; otherwise draft a supplementary declaration and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic submission to the INPI Guichet Unique and payment of registry fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), lodged for the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce and the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete M0 dossier via the secured portal and pay the droits de greffe and associated legalization fees electronically. The INPI forwards the dossier to the competent greffe, which performs the legality control and proceeds to RCS registration; the RNE then issues the registration attestation and the K-bis extract.
required_dossiers: Completed M0 dossier
Attestation de dépôt des fonds du capital
Attestation de parution de l'avis de constitution
Statuts certified by the legal representative
Declarations of non-bankruptcy and absence of judicial interdiction of the officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the greffe issues a query (demande de régularisation), provide the requested documents through the same portal within the prescribed deadline; if registration is refused, apply to the President of the Tribunal de Commerce for a gracieux review order per Articles R.123-92 and R.123-99 of the Code de commerce.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration formalities, K-bis extraction and opening of the operating bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / RNE; DGFiP and URSSAF through automatic notification generated by the registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon effective registration, obtain the RNE attestation and the extrait K-bis. The blocked capital deposit is released to the President against presentation of the K-bis. Verify the automatic allocation of the SIREN, SIRET, and TVA intracommunautaire numbers, submit the finalized notice to the JAL if required, and open the permanent company bank account using the K-bis.
required_dossiers: Extrait K-bis issued after registration
RNE registration attestation
Capital release certificate from the bank
SIREN/SIRET and VAT number notifications
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax or social identification numbers are not received automatically, contact the RNE support desk or the local DGFiP business registry office with the K-bis to obtain the SIREN, SIRET, and VAT numbers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de la Transition écologique et de la Cohésion des territoires — Direction Générale de l'Énergie et du Climat (DGEC); Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) for environmental permitting; Qualifelec as the national electrical works qualification body.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Qualification professionnelle Qualifelec (Référentiel NF 360 - Installations électriques) for the high-voltage contracting activity, accompanied by personnel electrical habilitation certificates under NF C18-510; where the substation is operated by the client, an Autorisation Environnementale (ICPE) or Déclaration ICPE for the high-voltage transformation site.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Inspection des Installations Classées (IIC) — DREAL, under the oversight of the Ministère de la Transition écologique et de la Cohésion des territoires.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category A1 — Full Environmental Impact Assessment (étude d'impact) required under Article L.122-1 and Annex R.122-2 of the French Environmental Code for high-voltage electrical infrastructure and associated ICPE installations, including a public inquiry (enquête publique) and a site-specific prévention plan.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: SF6 handling and leakage thresholds per Regulation (EU) No 517/2014 on fluorinated greenhouse gases (annual leak checks for equipment charged above 5 kg CO2 equivalent and maximum leakage rate of 0.5% per year for GIS); wastewater discharge standards for construction/operation sites under the general ICPE decree (pH 5.5–8.5; suspended solids MES ≤ 35 mg/L; COD ≤ 125 mg/L); PCB-free dielectric fluids for oil-filled equipment per Directive 96/59/EC; and exterior noise limit of 70 dB(A) at site boundaries during evening and night periods per the ministerial order of 23 January 1997.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the SDIS (Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours) including the permis de feu programme for hot works and the installation of fire barriers; structural load inspection by a registered bureau de contrôle covering the 500kV GIS hall floors, crane pads, and containment bunds; and occupational clearance delivered by a COFRAC-accredited electrical verifier confirming NF C18-510 habilitations, the plan de prévention per Décret n° 92-158, and emergency rescue coordination for live-voltage work.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP), French Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial Sovereignty; taxpayer portal: impots.gouv.fr; company registration formalities portal: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; registry: RCS via Infogreffe/INPI; customs excise and import/export portal: douane.gouv.fr with the DELTA declaration system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French SAS: (1) execute articles of association (statuts), publish the legal notice and file the incorporation dossier with the RCS through the Guichet des Formalités Entreprises; (2) after registration at the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, INSEE allocates the SIREN, which constitutes the corporate statutory tax ID, and the SIRET for each establishment; (3) DGFIP opens the income-tax/corporate-tax account and assigns the French VAT intra-Community identification number (format FR + two-digit key + SIREN); (4) if the SAS engages in cross-border trade, apply separately to customs for an EORI number (FR + SIREN). For a foreign entity without a French establishment performing taxable operations in France, no small-business VAT exemption is available: the non-EU entity must appoint a French tax representative (intermédiaire fiscal) and file a specific VAT registration application with DGFIP (Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères); EU-resident non-established suppliers may register directly and, where applicable, use OSS/IOSS for distance sales. The SIREN is the official TIN for filings; DGFIP does not issue a separate corporate tax ID.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (SAS is an independent legal entity, not pass-through; it is subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) under Article 205 CGI; the French territoriality principle under Article 209 CGI determines the taxable base for profits attributable to French operations; the SAS is a full IS taxpayer and has no transparent classification).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box or partnership pass-through election exists for an SAS. The SAS is by legal form subject to corporate-level taxation. Available elections include: (a) French tax consolidation (intégration fiscale) under Article 223 A et seq. CGI, elected by a French parent holding at least 95% of directly or indirectly held French subsidiaries; (b) parent-subsidiary participation exemption (régime mère-fille) under Articles 145 and 216 CGI, generally 95% exemption for qualifying dividends if the shareholding threshold and holding period are met; (c) OSS/IOSS elections for qualifying distance-selling supplies to final consumers; (d) for eligible infrastructure groups, the option for tax unity with a French head company. EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD) anti-hybrid rules are implemented in France and override contractual or entity classification mismatches; an SAS cannot elect transparent tax treatment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA), administered by the DGFIP for tax collection and by the French customs administration at importation and export.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For established small enterprises, no VAT registration is required until annual taxable turnover exceeds the franchise thresholds under Article 293 B CGI: EUR 85,800 for supplies of goods and EUR 37,300 for supplies of services (amounts periodically adjusted). Non-resident and non-established taxable persons have a zero threshold: they must register for French VAT before making their first taxable supply in France, including installation services for high-voltage substations on French immovable property.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France requires structured B2B e-invoicing on a phased statutory timetable: from 1 September 2026 all large enterprises must be able to receive and issue e-invoices, and from 1 September 2027 small and medium enterprises must issue e-invoices; all domestic B2B invoices must be transmitted through DGFIP-accredited dematerialisation partners (Plateformes de Dématérialisation Partenaires, PDPs) or the public platform (Portail Public de Facturation, PPF). The French system is a data-clearance and tax-analytics model: invoice data is reported to DGFIP in real time through the PDP/PPF network, but France does not apply a per-invoice digital stamp. Accepted structured formats are Factur-X, OASIS UBL and UN/CEFACT CII. Third-party software integrations must use certified API connections, and cross-border B2B transactions are reported through the separate e-reporting obligation. Non-resident suppliers with a French VAT account are also required to transmit their e-invoices/e-reporting data in accordance with this mandate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported outside the EU qualify for 0% VAT under Article 262-I-1° CGI if the supplier proves by customs and commercial transport records that the goods were actually dispatched or carried out of French/EU customs territory pursuant to a sale, and if the invoice, contract and payment conditions corroborate the export. Intra-EU dispatches to a VAT-registered customer also qualify at 0% under Article 262-I-2° when the customer's valid EU VAT ID is obtained and the recapitulative statement is filed. Services supplied to non-EU customers are outside French VAT where the place of supply is located outside France under the general cross-border B2B rule; however, services relating to French immovable property, including on-site design-build and installation of a high-voltage substation attached to land, are deemed supplied in France and are subject to 20% French VAT regardless of the customer's jurisdiction. The exporter must hold the complete documentary evidence package when filing the VAT return and retain it for the statutory retention period (generally six years).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (electronic Single Administrative Document/DELTA exit confirmation)
Bill of Lading or transport waybill (B/L, AWB, CMR or rail consignment note) evidencing physical movement outside France/EU
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank SWIFT statement evidencing receivable settlement
Commercial invoice and signed export sales contract
Packing list and export loading certificate
Certificate of non-EU destination or delivery receipt where required by French customs or the destination tax authority
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGFIP and the National Customs Intelligence Directorate (DNRED) cross-check DELTA export exit data against e-invoicing/e-reporting data, recapitulative statements and banking records. An unsupported or fraudulent export zero-rating claim is recharacterised: the VAT is clawed back at 20%, the exported input VAT is disallowed, refunded amounts are recovered and interest at 0.20% per month runs from the due date. Civil penalties are charged under Articles 1728 and 1729 CGI: 40% for non-intentional understatement, 80% for bad faith, abusive tax arrangement (abus de droit) or fraudulent documentation, and up to 100% for organised major fraud. Criminal prosecution under Article 1741 CGI may result in imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to EUR 500,000, and the French Code des Douanes may also impose forfeiture or confiscation of the goods and means of transport in cases of customs export fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, within the Eurosystem and subject to the monetary policy framework of the European Central Bank. French foreign-exchange and payment compliance also involves the French Treasury, the Directorate-General of Customs and Indirect Taxes, the French Financial Markets Authority, the French Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority, and Tracfin for anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing matters.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro, which is fully convertible for ordinary current-account transactions. France has no general exchange-control regime, no general approval requirement for cross-border payments, and no general restriction on repatriation of dividends, interest, royalties, loan principal, or liquidation proceeds. Capital-account transactions are generally permitted, subject to EU sanctions, anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing controls, foreign-investment screening, tax rules, corporate-law requirements, beneficial-ownership transparency, and bank-specific documentation. A French SAS may receive foreign equity, shareholder loans, and trade-related funds through regulated payment institutions or banks. Dividend and interest remittances require appropriate corporate approvals, distributable profits or valid debt documentation, withholding-tax analysis, transfer-pricing support where applicable, and evidence of the commercial purpose and beneficial recipient. Banks may delay or reject transfers involving sanctioned jurisdictions, opaque ownership, high-risk intermediaries, unexplained third-party payments, or incomplete source-of-funds evidence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no statutory requirement for a French company to repatriate export proceeds to France, surrender export receipts to a French bank, convert a prescribed percentage into euros, or complete conversion within a prescribed statutory period. Export receipts may generally remain in foreign-currency accounts or be received through foreign or European payment accounts, subject to contractual banking terms, accounting requirements, tax reporting, sanctions screening, customs and VAT documentation, and anti-money-laundering controls. Commercial banks may request invoices, transport documents, customs declarations, contracts, delivery evidence, and explanations for payment deviations. Foreign accounts and account income may trigger French tax reporting obligations, including annual reporting where applicable.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital deposit account for SAS incorporation or capital increase, followed by an operational current account with EUR and foreign-currency capabilities

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. and the relevant Crédit Agricole regional bank
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital deposit account and operational current account with domestic payment, SEPA, international wire, trade-finance, and foreign-exchange services
Capital deposit account, operating account, cash-management account, trade-finance account, and foreign-exchange dealing account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE group, including Banque Populaire or Caisse d'Epargne entities
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital deposit account and operating account with SEPA, SWIFT, treasury, and trade-finance functionality, subject to entity and branch acceptance
Operational business current account with EUR payment services; capital-deposit and advanced trade-finance availability must be confirmed with the relevant business-banking unit

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for routine operating payments and collections, but not a complete substitute for a French relationship bank. An electronic-money institution or payment institution licensed in France or another EEA state may provide payment accounts, SEPA transfers, cards, and certain foreign-currency services under passporting or local authorization. The provider must safeguard customer funds and may impose transaction, jurisdiction, or settlement limits. An offshore provider outside the EEA cannot lawfully provide regulated payment services in France without an applicable authorization, exemption, or licensed intermediary arrangement. A fintech account should not be assumed to satisfy French SAS incorporation-capital deposit requirements, bank guarantees, bid-bond requirements, lender covenants, public-procurement requirements, or commercial-letter-of-credit issuance requirements. Account continuity, safeguarding, insolvency protection, data location, transaction limits, sanctions controls, and access to SWIFT or correspondent banking must be contractually verified.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors physically attend a bank branch to open a corporate account. Remote onboarding may be permitted by the selected bank after electronic identity verification, video identification, qualified-signature procedures, and review of original or certified corporate documents. In practice, banks may require an in-person meeting or live video interview for non-resident shareholders, complex ownership chains, high-value expected flows, foreign directors, politically exposed persons, high-risk countries, unusual activities, or trade-finance facilities. The bank may require the legal representative, authorized signatories, ultimate beneficial owners, and controlling persons to complete individual identification. A notarial or bank capital-deposit account for an SAS may require additional original-document or certified-document procedures before issuance of the certificate of deposit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner with an opaque ownership chain, nominee arrangement, trust, bearer-equivalent control, or inconsistent ownership information
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current extract from the French commercial register after incorporation or a draft formation file; articles of association; shareholder register; ownership chart to each natural-person ultimate beneficial owner; passports and residential-address evidence; certificates of incorporation and registers for all intermediate entities; notarized or certified powers of attorney; beneficial-ownership filing evidence; and a written explanation of control rights.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of capital, shareholder loan funds, or initial operating liquidity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements; audited financial statements; tax returns; sale-of-business or investment agreements; board and shareholder resolutions; loan agreements; lender identity; proof of repayment terms; source-of-wealth memorandum; sanctions screening results; and a transaction-by-transaction funds-flow diagram showing the originating account, beneficial owner, purpose, and destination.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected high-value construction payments, milestone receipts, advance payments, retention amounts, or project accounts inconsistent with a newly incorporated entity's profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed customer and subcontractor contracts; tender awards; purchase orders; project budgets; milestone schedules; invoices; engineering or works specifications; delivery and acceptance certificates; expected monthly payment volumes; countries and counterparties matrix; cash-flow forecast; payment-approval policy; and reconciliation controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving subcontractors, agents, distributors, consultants, or beneficiaries located in multiple jurisdictions, particularly where third-party settlement is requested
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty legal documents; beneficial-ownership information; sanctions and PEP screening records; written commercial rationale; signed contracts; invoices; evidence of services; beneficial-payee confirmation; anti-bribery representations; commission calculations; tax and withholding analysis; and a policy prohibiting unexplained third-party payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Exposure to sanctioned countries, restricted persons, dual-use electrical equipment, public-sector customers, or projects requiring enhanced export-control review
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: End-user and end-use statements; project-country and customer screening; product classification; export-control assessment; sanctions-screening logs; licenses or governmental authorizations where required; contract sanctions clauses; shipping and customs documentation; and escalation records demonstrating legal review before payment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch among the stated activity, industry classification, contractual scope, and payment behavior, including unexpected trading, cryptocurrency, cash-intensive activity, or unrelated goods
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approved business plan; French registration and activity codes; statutory-license and professional-qualification evidence where applicable; organizational chart; project pipeline; insurance certificates; accounting engagement letter; written prohibited-activity policy; and management certification that account activity will be limited to electrical-substation installation and related lawful services.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically exposed person, close associate, adverse media, criminal-record concern, or regulatory investigation involving an owner, director, employee, agent, or major counterparty
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full identity and role description; independent adverse-media review; criminal-record or equivalent good-standing documentation where legally obtainable; explanation of historical matters; regulatory correspondence; enhanced due-diligence report; source-of-wealth evidence; compliance-officer approval; and documented enhanced transaction-monitoring procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Request for immediate international payments before the company has established normal operating history or before the bank has completed beneficial-ownership verification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formation timetable; capital-deposit certificate; signed customer or supplier contract; invoice and payment purpose; board authorization; proof of delivery or project necessity; expected transaction calendar; authorized-signatory matrix; and confirmation that no payment will be released until the bank's KYC and sanctions review is complete.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity contributions through a regulated French or EEA bank to an account held in the SAS's name or, before incorporation, to a qualifying capital-deposit account opened with a bank, notary, or Caisse des Dépôts mechanism where applicable. Use the investor's own bank account and identify the transfer as a capital contribution, share subscription, or shareholder loan. For an SAS formation or capital increase, retain the subscription form, shareholder or board resolution, articles or amendment, capital table, deposit certificate, Kbis or filing evidence, and proof of beneficial ownership. For a shareholder loan, retain a signed loan agreement, maturity, interest, repayment terms, transfer-pricing support where relevant, and evidence of the lender's authority. Use SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR payments within the SEPA area and SWIFT cross-border transfer for non-SEPA currencies or jurisdictions. France does not use a universal statutory foreign-exchange purpose-code system for ordinary corporate wires; provide a clear payment narrative in the transfer reference or SWIFT field 70 and comply with the receiving bank's internal purpose-code requirements. The receiving bank may request MT103 or ISO 20022 payment confirmation, originator and beneficiary information, source-of-funds evidence, and corporate authorizations. Reconcile the receipt to the capital or loan ledger and retain banking evidence for accounting, tax, audit, and AML purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible EUR supplier payments, subject to bank limits and beneficiary verification. Use SWIFT cross-border payments for non-SEPA currencies or counterparties; MT103 remains a commonly recognized customer-credit-transfer format, while banks are progressively migrating to ISO 20022 formats such as pacs.008. For significant equipment purchases, public-sector projects, unfamiliar counterparties, or jurisdictions presenting performance or country risk, use an irrevocable documentary commercial letter of credit, preferably subject to UCP 600, issued or confirmed by a reputable bank. Require defined presentation documents, including commercial invoice, packing list, transport document, certificate of origin, inspection certificate, insurance document, and installation or acceptance certificate where commercially appropriate. Use bank guarantees, advance-payment guarantees, performance guarantees, and retention guarantees where project contracts require them. Apply four-eyes payment approval, segregation of duties, beneficiary call-back verification, invoice and purchase-order matching, sanctions screening, duplicate-invoice controls, and payment-limit governance. Confirm VAT, withholding-tax, customs, import-control, and beneficial-payee requirements before settlement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/foreign-currency forward contracts with an authorized bank, used to hedge documented forecast or committed commercial exposures; apply written treasury mandates, maturity limits, counterparty limits, and underlying-exposure documentation.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies or jurisdictions where local convertibility or delivery is restricted, subject to bank availability, applicable market rules, sanctions screening, documentation of the underlying exposure, and EMIR, MiFID II, and regulatory-reporting requirements where applicable.

Currency swaps or cross-currency swaps for recurring funding, shareholder-loan, or long-dated project exposures, subject to ISDA or equivalent master documentation, collateral terms, valuation controls, counterparty credit limits, and applicable EMIR obligations.

Plain-vanilla currency options and collars for non-linear protection, subject to suitability, fair-value, premium, accounting, and governance controls; avoid speculative structures unrelated to identifiable business exposures.
Foreign-currency current accounts and natural hedging through matching receipts and payments in the same currency, subject to liquidity, concentration, and account-risk limits.

For an ordinary French SAS, derivatives should be used for risk reduction rather than proprietary speculation. The company should document the hedged item, hedge ratio, forecast certainty, tenor, counterparty, valuation method, accounting treatment, collateral exposure, and termination authority.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' meeting to approve financial statements (approbation des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records / Minutes register (not filed with a regulator)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct government fine, but failure to hold the meeting within the deadline exposes the company to court-ordered sanctions and invalidation of subsequent decisions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual financial statements with the commercial court registry (dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval by the shareholders' meeting and no later than 7 months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties: up to €3,000 per natural person and €15,000 per legal entity; the court may also impose periodic penalty payments (astreinte).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a fiscal year ending 31 December: 3 May of the following year; for any other fiscal year-end: within 3 months after year-end (4 months if filed online)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Immediate surcharge of 5% of the net tax due, increased to 10% if formal notice is required to file; additional monthly interest at 0.20%; criminal penalties for intentional non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business property tax (cotisation foncière des entreprises, CFE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on 15 December of the business year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 5% late-payment penalty plus monthly interest of 0.20%; administrative levy enforced after stringent collection procedure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation and update of the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: File with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce upon update; annual confirmation is performed internally
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually at the shareholders' meeting; any change in ownership must be registered with the RBE within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain an accurate UBO register or to update within the 30-day period can result in a criminal fine of up to €30,000 and/or imprisonment of up to 6 months.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit (commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory if the SAS exceeds at least two of these three thresholds at fiscal year-end: total assets exceeding €4,000,000; net turnover exceeding €8,000,000; average number of employees exceeding 50. Companies below the thresholds remain exempt unless the governance documents require an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP per Règlement ANC 2014-03 (PCG); IFRS as endorsed by the EU is allowed voluntarily for individual accounts and mandatory for consolidated accounts if applicable.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The register of beneficial owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) must be reconciled with the current share register at each annual shareholders' meeting. Any transfer of shares during the year must be recorded in the securities register and the UBO register concurrently updated within 30 days of the transfer. The annual confirmation is documented in the minutes of the shareholders' meeting.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard French corporate income tax rate
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday; reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for qualifying small enterprises with turnover at or below EUR 10 million; research tax credit (CIR) at 30% up to EUR 100 million of eligible R&D expenditure, 5% above; innovation tax credit (CII) at 20% for eligible SMEs; territorial provisions do not create a genuine tax holiday.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite no statutory time limit; however, annual offset of tax losses carried forward is capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the taxable profit exceeding EUR 1,000,000.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form CERFA 2065-SD (déclaration de résultats) together with annex schedules 2050 through 2059-FD; mandatory electronic filing via the impots.gouv.fr professional user portal or EDI/EFI exchange for companies subject to corporate income tax; non-resident companies with a French permanent establishment use Form 2065-SD plus 2065-RP (régime particulier).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. Quarterly instalments of corporate income tax are advance payments, not tax returns.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending on 31 December, the online filing deadline is generally 30 April of the following year, extended to the next business day where the portal closes; for other fiscal year-ends the return is due within 30 days after the close of the fiscal year, with a standard online accommodation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deducting allowable expenses, reincorporating non-deductible items, and applying accounting corrections; this is the base line for computing corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company must report only profits attributable to the French permanent establishment or to French-source income effectively connected with that establishment; attach Form 2065-RP where applicable and ensure the PE’s books are separately stated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year tax loss available for future offset, subject to statutory limitation and annual carryforward cap.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities may report a deficit only to the extent it is economically linked to the French PE and computed under French accounting and tax rules; all underlying records and local-file documentation should substantiate the loss.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2065-SD, annex / calculation of tax, case for crédits d’impôt and imputation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claimable tax credits, foreign tax credits on French-source income, reduced rates, and prepayments offset against the gross corporate income tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only credits attributable to the French PE or to income taxable in France may be claimed; shareholders do not include personal or parent-company tax credits on this return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 10% surcharge on the net tax payable; after formal notice the surcharge rises to 40%; fraudulent concealment or abusive behaviour attracts 80% penalties. In all cases monthly late-payment interest accrues at 0.20% of the unpaid principal. Failure to provide required annexes or documentation can trigger separate automatic fines.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% for dividends paid to non-resident corporate shareholders; 12.8% for non-resident individuals; 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for a qualifying parent company holding at least 5% of the French company for a minimum of two consecutive years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke Double Taxation Agreement relief, the beneficial owner must submit a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) and, where requested, Form 5000/5001 to the French paying agent before distribution. France requires proof of beneficial ownership, substance, and satisfaction of the treaty’s anti-abuse provisions (BEPS MLI principal-purpose test). Over-withheld tax may be reclaimed through the non-resident portal on impots.gouv.fr within the statutory time limit.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: generally 0% domestic withholding on debt interest paid to non-resident enterprises and financial institutions unless the payment benefits a non-cooperative jurisdiction. Royalties and intellectual property payments: statutory withholding of 33⅓% for patent and copyright royalties paid to non-residents, reduced to 15% for patented inventions; most French tax treaties reduce source-country royalty tax to 0%, 5%, or 10% depending on the type of royalty and beneficial-owner conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No automatic local-file filing threshold solely based on annual turnover in France. Upon administrative request, a Master File and Local File are mandatory when the controlled group’s consolidated revenue equals or exceeds EUR 400,000,000. Country-by-Country reporting is separately required where group consolidated revenue reaches EUR 750,000,000. An SAS below these thresholds should still keep transfer pricing documentation proportionate to the size and risk of its related-party transactions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a dedicated Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime in the same manner as some offshore centres; nevertheless, concepts of effective place of management, beneficial ownership, the anti-abuse doctrine under Livre des procédures fiscales Article L64, and the BEPS MLI principal-purpose test impose de facto substance requirements. A SAS must maintain premises, employees, real operational decision-making, and valid commercial records to preserve French tax residence and treaty access.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and intentional mis-declaration (CGI Art. 1741; LPF Art. L16)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate filing of a false corporate income tax return for high-voltage substation installation revenue, off-book invoicing, creation of fictitious subcontractors, or concealment of taxable income through cash or shell accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of the full tax understatement, interest for late payment, and penalty of 40% for bad faith or 80% for fraudulent concealment; criminal conviction carries imprisonment up to 5 years and a fine of EUR 500,000, increased to 7 years and EUR 3,000,000 in organised groups or where an artificial or overseas infrastructure is used to hide income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who knowingly signs or submits false accounts may be criminally prosecuted, personally ordered to pay restitution, prohibited from managing a company, subjected to travel bans where flight risk exists, and held civilly liable to creditors and the tax administration.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing documentation default and artificial pricing (LPF Arts. L13 AA, L13 B; CGI Art. 238A)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Cross-border invoicing between an SAS and a non-resident affiliate for engineering, labour, or milestone payments at a non-arm’s-length margin, or refusal to present the Global File/Local File after a formal audit request.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax administration may re-determine taxable income, reject the claimed deduction, apply market-based profit allocation, demand unpaid tax with monthly interest, and impose surcharges of up to 40% for insufficient declarations or 80% for organised abuse; separate fines can apply for failure to produce transfer pricing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who suppress documentation, approve sham contracts, or knowingly create unsubstantiated intercompany flows can be pursued for negligent management, required to satisfy unpaid corporate tax liabilities, and face criminal liability as accomplices to tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell-company structure and treaty abuse (abus de droit; BEPS MLI principal-purpose test)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of a zero-substance intermediary company to hold French substation contracts, redirect milestone payments, or accumulate dividends solely for treaty shopping rather than for genuine commercial purposes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Ignoring the intermediary, taxing the French beneficiary or the foreign corporate shareholder directly on the underlying income, denying treaty benefits, recharacterising the arrangement, and applying the 80% penalty for artificial abuse; the statutory time limit for reassessment can be extended to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorise or benefit from the artificial structure may be personally liable for restitution of avoided taxes, held in contempt for non-cooperation, banned from corporate office, prohibited from leaving the jurisdiction, and prosecuted for laundering the fiscal benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and beneficial ownership concealment (LCB-FT; Penal Code Arts. 324-1 et seq.)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Splitting large milestone wire transfers or letters of credit to bypass threshold reporting, routing payments through unidentified non-resident shell accounts, or knowingly failing to declare and update true beneficial owners of an SAS.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering is punishable by up to 5 years’ imprisonment and EUR 375,000 fine for an individual, increased to 10 years and EUR 750,000 for organised laundering; French AML authorities may also freeze funds, suspend bank transactions, and impose administrative sanctions against the corporate entity and its management.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who knowingly directs, structures, or hides suspicious payment flows is personally exposed to criminal penalties, confiscation of assets, travel bans, management bans, and civil claims for restitution; the corporate veil will be pierced where the director is the true actor behind the laundering arrangement.
